text: Multi-source ingestion, a correlation rule, a Conditional Access pilot, and an IR runbook -- then a real 3 AM alert that tested every piece of it.
The alert traced through CommonSecurityLog to a firewall rule scoped to 198.51.0.0/16 instead of the vendor's real 198.51.100.16/28, a gap present since the rule was created.
The rule was narrowed and validated with a positive and a negative test, then written into the runbook as a worked example with a new two-part standing control.
A vendor access rule written too broadly under deadline pressure, then never reviewed, is an ordinary, realistic cause of exposure -- exactly the kind of problem a working analyst actually finds.
The Advanced tier, built separately, carries this same discipline forward toward a board-level security review.
